messages:
alex: FYI seeing a steady p95 increase on canary since 02:10 UTC, ~15% over baseline. Requesting rollback guidance. :thinking:
maya: can you paste the canary slice and model/version?
alex: canary slice is 10% traffic west/eu, model = rw-infer/transformer-3 v3.5.0-canary. Logs show elevated decode latency around token 5-20.
jamie: any error spike or just latency?
alex: errors stable, just latency. Tail samples attached in thread (short). Looks correlated with new kernel selection on that build.
deploy-bot: Deploybot: AUTO-ROLLBACK decision: suppressed (conditions: error_rate<1%, latency_delta=+15% -> requires human review).
sre-oncall: +1 to human review. Need to check kv-cache hit rate and batching metrics before rollback. Can we snapshot metrics?
maya: grabbed a quick kpi: kvcache_hitrate=0.78 (down from 0.92), avg_batch_size unchanged. Might be a cache eviction regression from the new weight shape.
ops-lead: If kvcache_hit is the cause and errors are low, we can either: 1) pin traffic back to v3.4.2 (fast), 2) partial rollback of kernel flag only (safer), or 3) leave canary and increase telemetry window. Preference?
jamie: prefer pin to v3.4.2 for immediate mitigation. Prepare customer comms stub in case we need to notify enterprise customers.
alex: agree, pin seems fastest. Ops: how fast is a pin?
deploy-bot: Deploybot: RUNBOOK -> to pin run: 
```
POST /api/deploys/pin
{"model":"rw-infer/transformer-3","version":"v3.4.2","scope":"canary"}
```
expect ~90s to apply traffic rule, then 5-10m to observe stabilization.
sre-oncall: coordinate a quick smoke: run 50 synthetic calls through canary after pin and check p95.
maya: I'll draft the customer note: short blurb + ETA for full follow-up. Sending draft: 
"We observed elevated inference latency on a canary build affecting a small subset of traffic. We've pinned traffic to the previous model variant while we investigate. No user-facing errors expected. We'll share a post-mortem." :pencil: 
ops-lead: good. Also add internal release-note line: "rollback pin executed due to kv-cache hit regression; follow-up: kernel selection rollback candidate"
jamie: ok ops, please proceed with pin; alex and maya run the verification and keep this thread updated.
alex: starting pin now. tagging @deploy-bot for run. :rocket:
deploy-bot: Deploybot: PIN applied to canary (v3.4.2). Change id: change-1765439999-01.
alex: running smoke now. 1/50 -> ok, 25/50 -> p95 back within baseline.
maya: customer note sent to enterprise-notify channel draft for approvals.
sre-oncall: monitoring for 15m, if stable we close and open follow-up ticket for kernel/kv investigation.
ops-lead: thumbs up. Once follow-up ticket exists, include rolling plan for dedicated pools and docs for pin rollback procedure. :thumbsup:
jamie: thanks team. Postmortem template: include metric deltas, sample prompts, kernel diff, and release note update.
alex: closing updates: canary stabilized at 03:05 UTC. Opening ticket RW-1429 for kernel/kv root cause and test to prevent regressing cache hitrate.
maya: tagging support to be ready if customers ping. :bell:
ops-lead: will draft short internal tl;dr and mark release notes. Good job. :white_check_mark:
